title: Interaction coefficients have their own consistency equation
question: When direct and indirect paths carry opposing treatment-by-covariate interactions, does the pooled network meta-regression mask the modifier while the effect-consistency check passes, and can an interaction-consistency check detect it?
design: Triangle networks with path-specific interaction slopes (consistent, partly opposing, cancelling), two to eight studies per comparison, two covariate spreads and effect inconsistency absent or present; consistency meta-regression, modifier selection, interaction and effect consistency checks. 36 cells, 2000 replicates each.
answer: Opposing interactions on direct and indirect paths attenuate the pooled network meta-regression interaction toward zero, fully at the balance point and partly across a continuum, while the effect-consistency check stays at its null rate. The target effect was biased by 0.13 to 0.30 whether or not the covariate was selected. A direct interaction-consistency check detects it when studies per path and covariate spread are adequate (up to 1.00) and has little power otherwise (0.16 with two studies and narrow spread).
findings: Effect-consistency check flag rate 0.094 to 0.107 in every interaction-inconsistent scenario without effect inconsistency (blindness confirmed).
Refuting sentence fails: partly opposing interactions biased the target by -0.13 to -0.26.

Cancelling configuration: pooled interaction mean near 0 but replicate SD 0.13 to 0.67 against model SE 0.03 to 0.38 (1.5 to 4.2 times), so the Wald test selected the covariate in 31% to 88% of analyses.
Interaction-consistency check power 0.16 to 1.00, rising with studies per comparison and covariate spread.
not_answered: Stylized triangles with continuous estimates; design-by-treatment interaction model and larger networks not run. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: C versus A effect at a covariate value of 1.5, with the AC path's modification as truth
methods_compared: consistency network meta-regression with covariate selection
